key_insight: A self-supervised functional autoencoder learns a reusable latent space, separating function representation from task-specific operator learning.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics surrogates, frozen representations can reduce training memory and time while supporting fields sampled on arbitrary point clouds.
method: Pre-train on analytically generated functions without solvers or labels.
Freeze translation-, dilation-, and amplitude-equivariant representation maps and cache dataset embeddings.
Train task-specific neural operators in latent space and decode predicted fields.
evidence_signal: Across 28 tasks spanning solid mechanics and other PDE domains, the abstract reports accuracy that can exceed state-of-the-art end-to-end models, up to 10× higher throughput, and chunked inference on over half a billion points.
watch_item: Accuracy and efficiency gains should be verified for the target mechanics regime; the abstract does not establish performance for every material law or boundary condition.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
